# Reduce

Combines the elements of an array into one value, by a lambda applied to each element in turn.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Reduce(items, callback, initial)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to read, which is left unchanged. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `callback` | function | A lambda of exactly two parameters: the first receives the value combined so far (initial, for the first element), and the second receives the element. Its result, of any type, null included, is the value combined so far for the next element. A lambda of any other number of parameters, or a value that is not a lambda, null included, is a runtime error. |
| `initial` | any | The value to start from, of any type, null included. It must be given. |

## Returns

Any. The lambda's result for the last element, or initial when items is empty. Null when that value is null: when the last result of the lambda is null, or when items is empty and initial is null.

## Remarks

The lambda is called once for each element, in order. It is given the elements the array holds when the call starts, so a change the lambda makes to the array does not change which elements it is given.

## Example

`Reduce([1, 2, 3], (total, x) => total + x, 0)` returns 6.
